ic_name: ARM Serial Wire Debug (SWD) — ADIv5 (ARM IHI 0031C)
fsm_summary: SWD wire-level state machine sequences each 46-bit transaction through 6 phases (Request → Turnaround → ACK → Data → Parity → Turnaround). The target's SW-DP shift register is driven by SWCLK rising edges; SWDIO direction (host-driven vs target-driven) flips at the Turnaround periods. Independent of the transaction state machine, the SW-DP top-level state recognizes the 50-cycle line-reset sequence (50 SWCLKs with SWDIO=1) and returns to the reset state from anywhere. The SWJ-DP variant adds a mode-select state machine that watches for the 16-bit JTAG-to-SWD (0xE79E) and SWD-to-JTAG (0xE73C) selection sequences and switches between SWD and JTAG protocol stacks.

fsm_states_swd_transaction.name: Idle
fsm_states_swd_transaction.description: Between transactions. SWDIO is host-driven HIGH (no activity).

fsm_states_swd_transaction.name: RequestRx
fsm_states_swd_transaction.description: Target shifts in the 8-bit Request packet on SWDIO rising edges (host-driven). Bits 0..7: Start, APnDP, RnW, A[2], A[3], Parity, Stop, Park.

fsm_states_swd_transaction.name: RequestDecode
fsm_states_swd_transaction.description: Target validates: Start=1, Stop=0, Park=1, and even parity over APnDP+RnW+A[2:3]. On parity error, target ignores the transaction and may return WAIT or all-zeros on subsequent transactions until line reset.

fsm_states_swd_transaction.name: TurnaroundA
fsm_states_swd_transaction.description: Direction-change cycle: host releases SWDIO; target prepares to drive ACK.

fsm_states_swd_transaction.name: ACK_Drive
fsm_states_swd_transaction.description: Target drives the 3-bit ACK on SWDIO falling edges (host samples on rising edges).

fsm_states_swd_transaction.name: DataDrive_Read
fsm_states_swd_transaction.description: For RnW=1 (read) + ACK=OK: target drives 32 data bits on SWDIO falling edges (LSB first).

fsm_states_swd_transaction.name: DataDrive_Write
fsm_states_swd_transaction.description: For RnW=0 (write) + ACK=OK: host drives 32 data bits on SWDIO rising edges (LSB first). Target samples and accumulates parity.

fsm_states_swd_transaction.name: ParityDrive_Read
fsm_states_swd_transaction.description: For reads: target drives the 33rd bit = parity of the 32 data bits.

fsm_states_swd_transaction.name: ParityDrive_Write
fsm_states_swd_transaction.description: For writes: host drives the 33rd bit = parity of the 32 data bits. Target checks and sets WDATAERR on mismatch.

fsm_states_swd_transaction.name: TurnaroundB
fsm_states_swd_transaction.description: Direction-change cycle: target releases SWDIO; host prepares to drive next Request.

fsm_states_swd_transaction.name: WaitOrFault
fsm_states_swd_transaction.description: For ACK=WAIT or ACK=FAULT: target drives 32 zeros (or undefined) on SWDIO during the Data phase. Host must ignore the data and either retry (WAIT) or abort+retry (FAULT).

fsm_states_swd_transaction.name: LineResetDetect
fsm_states_swd_transaction.description: Top-level detector — counts consecutive SWCLK cycles with SWDIO=HIGH; on 50+ cycles, asynchronously forces the wire-level FSM back to Idle and clears the DP shadow state.

fsm_states_swj_dp_mode_select.name: JTAG_Mode
fsm_states_swj_dp_mode_select.description: SWJ-DP is in JTAG mode — JTAG TAP FSM and SWD FSM both watch the same pads; SWD watch is gated off; JTAG TAP responds to TMS/TCK as usual.

fsm_states_swj_dp_mode_select.name: WatchSWDSelect
fsm_states_swj_dp_mode_select.description: After ≥ 50 cycles of TMS=1, the SWJ-DP starts watching the next 16 TMS bits for the JTAG-to-SWD pattern 0xE79E (LSB first on TMS).

fsm_states_swj_dp_mode_select.name: SWD_Mode
fsm_states_swj_dp_mode_select.description: SWJ-DP has switched to SWD mode — JTAG TAP is gated off; SWD FSM is active on SWCLK/SWDIO (= TCK/TMS pads).

fsm_states_swj_dp_mode_select.name: WatchJTAGSelect
fsm_states_swj_dp_mode_select.description: After ≥ 50 cycles of SWDIO=1 in SWD mode, the SWJ-DP starts watching the next 16 SWDIO bits for the SWD-to-JTAG pattern 0xE73C (LSB first).

fsm_hints.clock: SWCLK is host-driven and free-running during a transaction; idle level is host-defined. Target samples SWDIO on rising edges during host-driven phases.
fsm_hints.sampling_edge: Target samples SWDIO on SWCLK rising edge during Request and Data-Write phases.
fsm_hints.drive_edge: Target drives SWDIO on SWCLK falling edge during ACK and Data-Read phases (so the host can sample cleanly on the next rising edge).
fsm_hints.abort: 50 consecutive SWCLK cycles with SWDIO=HIGH = line reset; any in-flight transaction is aborted and SW-DP returns to Idle. A subsequent IDCODE/DPIDR read is required.
fsm_hints.transaction_overlap: Posted reads: the data of read N is delivered with the ACK of read N+1. The final read in a burst is recovered via DP.RDBUFF.
fsm_hints.instruction_change_path: Switching from a DP transaction to an AP transaction requires writing DP.SELECT first (to set APSEL+APBANKSEL); subsequent AP transactions then go to the indexed AP register window.

anti_deadlock_rule: 50-cycle line reset (SWDIO held HIGH for ≥ 50 SWCLK cycles) is the universal escape — there is no SWD state from which this sequence does not return to the Idle/reset state. This guarantees the host can always recover SWD without power-cycling the target.
exit_from_reset_or_poweron: On power-up, the SW-DP starts in a quiescent state; the host's first action is a 50-cycle line reset followed by an IDCODE/DPIDR read. On line reset, SELECT and CTRL/STAT are cleared, the AP selection state resets to APSEL=0/APBANKSEL=0, and the posted-read queue is drained. The DPIDR value is hard-wired and always available.

default_ready_state_recommendation.SWCLK: Idle level not specified; debug probe drives. Most probes leave SWCLK low between transactions.
default_ready_state_recommendation.SWDIO: Idle level HIGH (line-reset compatible). Debug probes typically drive SWDIO high during idle to keep the target in a clean state.

configurations.name: Single-target SWD
configurations.description: One SoC on the SWD bus; host directly drives SWCLK/SWDIO.

configurations.name: Multi-drop SWD
configurations.description: Two or more SoCs share SWDIO/SWCLK; per-target selection via DP TARGETSEL transaction after a line reset + JTAG-to-SWD sequence (ADIv5.2).

configurations.name: SWJ-DP mode-switched
configurations.description: SoC supports both SWD and JTAG; mode is selected at runtime via 16-bit selection sequences on SWDIO/TMS pad.

timing_dependency_rule: All transaction-state-machine transitions are synchronous to SWCLK. Target drives SWDIO on the falling edge during target-driven phases; host samples on the rising edge. Setup/hold of SWDIO relative to SWCLK rising edge is per-device. The 50-cycle line-reset detector is also synchronous to SWCLK rising edges.

swd_to_jtag_mode_switching.selection_sequence_preconditions: Both selection sequences must be preceded by ≥ 50 cycles of SWDIO/TMS=HIGH (line reset in the current mode) and followed by ≥ 50 cycles of SWDIO/TMS=HIGH (line reset in the new mode).
